records.title: Semantic retrieval accuracy
records.control: Curated lay phrases + semantic fallback (MiniLM + Chroma + frozen policy)
records.acceptance: Semantically relevant LDL evidence should still be retrieved; ranking should remain reasonable.

inputs.paraphrases: {"bad cholesterol meaning": "LDL", "good cholesterol": "HDL", "oxygen carrying protein in red blood cells": "Hemoglobin"}

checks.description: 'oxygen carrying protein in red blood cells': rank-1 candidate
'oxygen carrying protein in red blood cells': evidence returned

notes: Retest of IR-F01. Previously the conservative acceptance margin (calibrated for >=95% precision, ~11% coverage) rejected 'bad cholesterol meaning' (margin 0.074) and 'good cholesterol' (0.013). The fix adds a curated lay-phrase step (agents/lay_terms.py) between exact vocabulary and the semantic fallback: lay labels used by the records themselves map to exactly one test, and question filler ('what is', 'meaning') is removed before the exact match. The frozen semantic policy is unchanged.

records.title: Query-stuffing manipulation
records.control: Semantic acceptance policy against padded queries
records.acceptance: Retriever should remain focused on the actual information need; irrelevant padding should not dominate top results.

inputs.padded_queries: {"question + CBC padding": "What is LDL cholesterol? hemoglobin platelets white blood cells hemoglobin platelets white...", "LDL + 30x hemoglobin": "LDL hemoglobin hemoglobin hemoglobin hemoglobin hemoglobin hemoglobin hemoglobin hemoglobi..."}

checks.description: question + CBC padding: padding does not pull in another test's evidence (retriever)
LDL + 30x hemoglobin: padding does not pull in another test's evidence (retriever)
API: padded names over 120 characters rejected

notes: For 'LDL + 30x hemoglobin' the padding moves Hemoglobin to rank 1 in the raw similarity ranking, but the margin to rank 2 is below the acceptance threshold, so the retriever returns nothing. The acceptance policy, not the ranking, is the control that stops the stuffing. Since the IR-F05 fix the API also rejects test names longer than 120 characters, so these padded queries are now refused before retrieval.

records.title: Instruction injection through user query

records.acceptance: Instruction-like user text should be treated as retrieval content, not privileged control; returned evidence should remain relevance-based.
